name: watering hole
description: A race to one water hole, played with both players moving at once. On a 7x7 board White's elephants and cats face Black's dogs and rats, every animal stepping one square in any direction, and the four kinds form a rock-paper-scissors chain across the two armies: elephant eats dog, dog eats cat, cat eats rat, rat eats elephant. Each of your animals hunts one enemy kind and flees the other. Each round both players choose a move in secret and both are made together; two animals stepping onto one square meet and the eater wins, while a hunter stepping where its prey has just left finds it empty. The first animal to stand on the hole at d4 with none of its eaters next to it wins, and almost every game is won there. Everything turns on the guess: step toward the hole and you may walk into the one animal that eats you, hold back to guard it and the other side may slip through. The armies differ on purpose: no meeting is ever two of a kind, so none ends in a tie.

provenance.source: docs/archive/plan-simultaneous.md, Q918e: a game designed around simultaneous moves
provenance.history: Q918e (2026-10-15), the showcase of schema 26's rules.simultaneous.tie impossible and the game designed around guessing that docs/archive/plan-simultaneous.md §6.8 asks for: a four-kind food chain split between two armies, so every meeting has a winner, and one shared goal square, so two arrivals in one round are a meeting and not a draw. Drafts v1 to v7 and why each changed are in docs/archive/plan-simultaneous.md, Q918e. Pre-registered there before it was measured. Joined the library from preview by Q934 (2026-10-17): the library's first game played in rounds and its only one with no royal, in which two arrivals on the one shared square are a meeting that always has a winner, so no game is drawn; viable 4-0 at 0.608 on the round roster (Q944a).
